# Clauses this repository must keep carrying. One per line:
#
#     path/to/file :: text that must appear somewhere in it
#
# `#` starts a comment only at the beginning of a line, because a clause is a
# fragment of prose and markdown headings begin with one. Whitespace is
# collapsed on both sides before matching, so a rewrap is not a policy change.
#
# Pin the shortest fragment that cannot survive the deletion you are guarding
# against. Retiring a clause is a deliberate act: do it in its own commit, so
# the decision is visible in the history rather than in a merge nobody read.
#
# Not a workflow's behaviour. Pinning a step by its text is a category error:
# deleting the step and leaving a comment that quotes it satisfies the clause,
# and a fragment that occurs twice stays satisfied by the other copy when one
# step is deleted. `check-aggregate-covers-jobs`-style coverage is what guards a
# deleted job; a deleted step is guarded by nothing here, and that is stated
# rather than papered over.

# ── the attribution rule ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A merge that takes `main..branch` as a stale branch's residue can delete this
# rule with every check green: the attribution gate scans tracked files for the
# vendor name and has no opinion about the policy mandating it going away.
AGENTS.md :: ## Assistant attribution — hard rule
AGENTS.md :: Never name an AI assistant, its vendor, or a model

# ── the supply-chain cap ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The same stale-residue merge can revert it. Without it `patterns: ['*']`
# collects majors into the weekly bundle. Note the single quotes: this clause
# pins YAML syntax, so a reformatting of that file needs it re-pinned.
.github/dependabot.yml :: update-types: ['minor', 'patch']
